title: Canada Holds Student Arrivals Target at Up to 150,000 a Year Through 2029
excerpt: IRCC's 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan extends the student target into 2029 and holds total new temporary resident arrivals at 370,000 a year — while actual student arrivals run at about half the target.
body:
• Canada's 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, released by IRCC alongside Budget 2026 on November 5, 2026, holds the target at up to 150,000 new international student arrivals a year — and extends it to 2029, a year the previous plan had not covered.
  • Counted here: new student and worker arrivals only. Not counted: permit extensions, in-Canada study or work permit applications, and visitors. The 2028 and 2029 figures are notional and will be confirmed or adjusted by November 1 of next year.
  • India is Canada's largest source of students: 94,025 study permits that became effective in 2025 were for Indian nationals, 24.6% of the total, according to IRCC's annual report to Parliament.
  • Arrivals are running far below the target — 115,180 new students arrived in 2025 against a target of 305,900 — so the 150,000 figure is a ceiling on new arrivals, not a forecast of how many students will come.

Canada will keep its target of up to 150,000 new international student arrivals a year through 2029, after Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) extended the figure into a third year in its 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan. The plan, released alongside the federal budget on November 5, 2026, holds annual new temporary resident arrivals at 370,000 in each of 2027, 2028 and 2029 — 150,000 students and 220,000 workers — and keeps permanent resident admissions at 380,000 a year.

Who is affected

The student target covers foreign nationals arriving in Canada to study for six months or more at a designated learning institution (DLI), the schools approved by provincial and territorial governments to host international students. It is a target for new arrivals. It does not count students already in Canada who extend a study permit, people who apply for a permit from inside Canada, or visitors. The worker side of the 370,000 splits into 170,000 arrivals through the International Mobility Program and 50,000 through the Temporary Foreign Worker Program, according to IRCC's supplementary information for the plan.

What changed — and what did not

The 150,000 student figure itself is not new. Last year's plan had already set it for 2027 and 2028; what the 2027–2029 plan changes is the horizon, carrying the same targets into 2029 and giving institutions a three-year planning window. Permanent resident admissions stay at 380,000 a year, with the economic class above 64% of the total, and IRCC says it wants permanent admissions below 1% of the population beyond 2027. One qualifier matters for anyone planning around the later years: IRCC's own table notes that the targets and ranges for 2028 and 2029 are notional, to be confirmed or adjusted by November 1 of next year.

For 2026, the target for new study permits was 155,000, according to ICEF Monitor's analysis of the plan. The new plan therefore holds the student intake essentially flat rather than cutting it further — a shift from the steep reductions of the past two years, when the new-arrivals target fell from 305,900 students in 2025 to the current level.

The gap between the target and actual arrivals

The target is not the binding constraint right now; demand and processing are. IRCC's annual report to Parliament recorded 115,180 new international student arrivals in 2025, against a target of 305,900 for that year, and total temporary arrivals of 323,995 against a planned range of 604,900 to 742,400. Study permits that became effective in 2025 — a broader measure that includes extensions — fell 26.1% to 381,725, and student transitions to permanent residence fell 18.7% to 20,790.

The 2026 figures point the same way. The Canadian Bureau for International Education (CBIE), welcoming the plan's stability, noted that Canada welcomed just over 65,000 new international student arrivals between January and August 2026, putting the country on track to reach only about half of its annual target by year-end. Within the smaller flow, the mix is shifting toward graduate study: master's and doctoral students, who were exempted from the study permit cap in January 2026, accounted for 20% of new study permits issued between January and August 2026, nearly double their 12% share in 2025, according to ICEF Monitor.

What to do next

For an Indian student planning a 2027 start, nothing in this plan changes the application itself: you still apply for a study permit to a designated learning institution, and the plan announces no new application cap for 2027. What it changes is the planning horizon — the intake ceiling is now set through 2029, and the competition it creates is for the strongest applications, particularly at the graduate level, rather than for a shrinking number of places. Universities Canada welcomed the three consistent years, saying predictable policies are essential to rebuilding confidence in Canada's international education system. Read the full target tables in IRCC's supplementary information before relying on any single figure, and treat the 2028 and 2029 numbers as notional until IRCC confirms them.
